task.title: Inspect recurrence provenance by task through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/897 by exposing exact recurrence provenance lookup by task identity through deterministic read-only CLI JSON.
acceptance_criteria: Validate task identity before storage access and open only an existing database read-only.
Emit complete materialized occurrence JSON for a binding and explicit null for an unrelated task.
Fail closed with deterministic escaped diagnostics for selected corruption or ambiguous bindings.

attempts.diagnostic: CLI integration tests failed with unrecognized subcommand task.
attempts.patch: Added focused integration coverage for the acceptance contract before adding production behavior.

attempts.diagnostic: Added recurrence task, delegated exact lookup to RecurrenceStore::find_materialized_by_task_id, and reused materialized-occurrence serialization.
attempts.patch: Added recurrence task, delegated exact lookup to RecurrenceStore::find_materialized_by_task_id, and reused materialized-occurrence serialization.

attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit found that corruption setup could pass without proving both SQL updates ran and could accept the wrong error category. Commit 665b39a split the updates, asserted one affected row each, and required the replay-error prefix; CodeRabbit confirmed the finding addressed.
attempts.patch: Kept replay, ambiguity, and provenance policy in the kernel while sharing the existing complete JSON projection. Reran the complete repository quality gate after the exact implementation state was ready.

outcome.summary: Operators can inspect one task identity for complete recurrence provenance without mutating storage or broadening scheduler authority.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0179-recurrence-provenance-by-identity-cli.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 185 records: 185 valid, 0 invalid

lessons: Corruption tests must assert fixture mutations actually affected the intended rows or they can pass for the wrong durable state.
Failure assertions should prove the intended replay taxonomy rather than accept any high-level command failure.
CLI adapters should validate identity before storage access and delegate provenance policy to the kernel.
An explicit null is deterministic absence evidence, not authority to create or execute work.
